cards.title: Open problem: Exact Hausdorff dimension of Liouville quantum gravity
cards.body:
OPEN PROBLEM from the Codex campaign ledger (source_says_open; current status unverified; result status unsolved). Determine the almost sure Hausdorff dimension d_gamma of the gamma-LQG metric for general gamma in (0,2), beyond the known value4 at gamma=sqrt(8/3). Source: Rhodes-Vargas: Two decades of probabilistic approach to Liouville conformal field theory,2025, Section3,PDF4.
Posed in Rhodes-Vargas: Two decades of probabilistic approach to Liouville conformal field theory,2025

cards.title: Attempt on Exact Hausdorff dimension of Liouville quantum gravity
cards.body:
ATTEMPT RECORD from the Codex campaign (author-checked by that worker only). Method: Explicit calculation or obstruction with source-specific scope Result: Constant shifts of the field multiply quantum area by exp(gamma*c) and metric distances by exp(xi*c), where xi is the metric scaling parameter. If a metric-volume exponent d is identified consistently with these scalings, the necessary relation is xi*d=gamma. This reproduces d=4 when xi=gamma/4 at the Brownian-map parameter. It does not calculate xi for other parameters. Check: The two scaling laws give the same volume rescaling only if exp(xi*d*c)=exp(gamma*c) for every real c. Merely inserting the smooth-metric exponent gamma/2 would force d=2 and contradict the known Brownian value. Obstruction: The missing quantity is the nontrivial first-passage metric normalization exponent, together with the theorem relating metric-ball volumes to it. Gaussian multiplicative chaos moments determine quantum area multifractality but do not supply the metric exponent. No new dimension formula is established.
